conclusion: Black rot caused by Guignardia bidwellii produces lesions and attacks leaves, stems, fruits, and roots.
Primary inoculum is released during flowering with rain, consistent inoculum loads are needed, models are discussed, and incidence is rising.
Rain during flowering, climate change, and temperature influence infection and control efficacy.

Molecular and proteomic analyses reveal two species, a draft genome is available, dioxolanones act as virulence factors, spore adhesion depends on wettability, and fungicide sensitivity range is narrow.
Genetic determinants of grapevine resistance are reviewed and breeding of resistant varieties is advocated.

Sanitation (hand pruning) can prevent disease; myclobutanil gives complete lesion control, azoxystrobin partial control; field trials show 65–76.7% efficacy, untreated vines lose >70% yield; integrated strategies are recommended.
